title: Walmart Enters the Gun Control Debate

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的日报通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、扎伊尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的现场对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The nation's largest retailer says it will stop selling the kinds of bullets used by mass shooters and call on Congress to consider a new ban on assault rifles.
sentences.zh: 全美最大的零售商表示，将停止销售大规模枪击事件中使用的那种子弹，并呼吁国会考虑颁布新的攻击性武器禁令。

sentences.en: Financial columnist
sentences.zh: 财经专栏作家

sentences.en: Andrew Ross-Sorkin on why corporate America is now in the business of regulating guns.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金将讲述为何美国企业界现在开始涉足枪支监管。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, September 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月5日，星期四。

sentences.en: Andrew, tell me about this email that you got.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，跟我说说你收到的那封邮件。

sentences.en: So sitting at my desk, it's midday Tuesday, actually about to get up to go grab lunch.
sentences.zh: 当时我正坐在办公桌前，那是周二中午，我正准备起身去吃午饭。

sentences.en: And I looked at my screen and an email popped up and it said from Doug McMillan.
sentences.zh: 我看着屏幕，弹出一封邮件，发件人是道格·麦克米伦。

sentences.en: Now Doug McMillan is the CEO of Walmart, the largest retailer in the country.
sentences.zh: 道格·麦克米伦是沃尔玛的首席执行官，也是全国最大的零售商。

sentences.en: And the subject line was Walmart's next steps.
sentences.zh: 邮件主题是“沃尔玛的下一步行动”。

sentences.en: And he started the email, Dear Andrew, I wanted to follow back up with you on the subject of firearms and ammunition.
sentences.zh: 他在邮件开头写道：“亲爱的安德鲁，我想就枪支和弹药的问题与你进行后续沟通。”

sentences.en: And my eyes widened.
sentences.zh: 我顿时瞪大了眼睛。

sentences.en: And what does it actually say?
sentences.zh: 那邮件里到底说了什么？

sentences.en: So he lays out a multi-part plan in the wake of this terrible massacre that had taken place at a
sentences.zh: 在埃尔帕索一家沃尔玛门店发生造成22人死亡的惨案后，他制定了一项多部分的计划，

sentences.en: Walmart store in El Paso, which 22 people were killed, about how Walmart is going to move forward and what steps they're going to take to try to end gun violence.
sentences.zh: 阐述了沃尔玛将如何推进工作，以及他们将采取哪些措施来试图终结枪支暴力。

sentences.en: And he says, one, we're going to stop selling certain kind of ammunition, the kind of ammunition that's often used in military-style
sentences.zh: 他说，第一，我们将停止销售某些类型的弹药，即那种经常用于军用风格

sentences.en: weapons, the AR-15 style weapons that you hear so much about that are used in these mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 武器的弹药，也就是你经常听到的、在这些大规模枪击事件中使用的AR-15式武器。

sentences.en: He also says, we're going to stop selling handgun ammunition completely.
sentences.zh: 他还说，我们将完全停止销售手枪弹药。

sentences.en: In addition to all that, though, and maybe even more importantly, he says, Walmart is going to advocate that lawmakers
sentences.zh: 除此之外，也许更重要的是，他说沃尔玛将倡导立法者

sentences.en: have a robust debate about reinstating the assault weapon ban.
sentences.zh: 就恢复攻击性武器禁令进行充分辩论。

sentences.en: And in addition to that, says that Walmart is going to advocate for the government to fund research into gun violence.
sentences.zh: 此外，他还表示沃尔玛将倡导政府资助对枪支暴力的研究。

sentences.en: These are big steps.
sentences.zh: 这些都是重大举措。

sentences.en: For Walmart, these are very big steps.
sentences.zh: 对于沃尔玛来说，这些是非常重大的举措。

sentences.en: And unbeknownst to me, 20 minutes later,
sentences.zh: 而且我当时并不知道，20分钟后，

sentences.en: Walmart is putting out a series of statements.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛将发布一系列声明。

sentences.en: And this email was effectively a heads up that this was about to happen.
sentences.zh: 这封邮件实际上是一个预告，告知这些事情即将发生。

sentences.en: Breaking news now from the world's largest retailer, Walmart, just announced...
sentences.zh: 突发新闻，全球最大零售商沃尔玛刚刚宣布……

sentences.en: Walmart says it will no longer sell ammunition for handguns or for short-barreled rifles.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛表示将不再销售手枪或短管步枪的弹药。

sentences.en: The ammo can be used in assault-style weapons.
sentences.zh: 这些弹药可用于攻击性武器。

sentences.en: Additionally, Walmart asking customers to no longer carry guns into its stores in open-carry states.
sentences.zh: 此外，沃尔玛还要求顾客在允许公开携带枪支的州，不要携带枪支进入其门店。

sentences.en: In a memo to employees, CEO Doug McMillan saying, quote, we've also been listening to a lot of people inside and outside our company as we think
sentences.zh: 在给员工的备忘录中，首席执行官道格·麦克米伦写道：“我们也在倾听公司内外许多人的意见，思考

sentences.en: about the role we can play in helping to make the country safer.
sentences.zh: 我们能在帮助国家变得更安全方面发挥什么作用。”

sentences.en: It's clear to us that the status quo is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，现状显然是不可接受的。

sentences.en: And Andrew, why is the CEO of Walmart sending this email with these plans to you before he makes it public to the rest of the world?
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，为什么沃尔玛首席执行官在向世界其他地方公开这些计划之前，先要把这封邮件发给你？

sentences.en: Well, oddly enough, this story actually starts over a year and a half ago.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说来奇怪，这个故事其实始于一年半前。

sentences.en: Now to the latest on the most recent deadly school shooting in America.
sentences.zh: 现在回到美国最近发生的致命校园枪击案的最新消息。

sentences.en: A gunman armed with an AR-15 semi-automatic rifle and carrying multiple magazines went on a deadly rampage at a high school in Parkland, Florida.
sentences.zh: 一名持AR-15半自动步枪并携带多个弹匣的枪手在佛罗里达州帕克兰的一所高中进行了致命的疯狂扫射。

sentences.en: After the mass shooting at the high school in Parkland, Florida.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州帕克兰的高中发生大规模枪击事件之后。

sentences.en: 17 people are dead.
sentences.zh: 17人死亡。

sentences.en: 14 other victims remain in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 另有14名受害者仍在医院接受治疗。

sentences.en: And after that shooting, there really felt like there was a moment.
sentences.zh: 在那次枪击事件之后，真的感觉出现了一个转折点。

sentences.en: Well, unprecedented and powerful tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚的情况前所未有且充满力量。

sentences.en: There are plans to do more.
sentences.zh: 有计划要做更多的事情。

sentences.en: There was a huge activist movement in this country.
sentences.zh: 这个国家出现了一场巨大的激进运动。

sentences.en: Young Americans took to the streets today in numbers likely not seen since the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 今天，年轻的美国人走上街头，人数之多可能是越战以来未见的。

sentences.en: The March for Our Lives was a response to the massacre last month.
sentences.zh: “为我们的生命游行”是对上个月那场大屠杀的回应。

sentences.en: In a little over six minutes, 17 of our friends were taken from us, 15 were injured, and everyone, absolutely everyone, in the Douglas community was forever altered.
sentences.zh: 在短短六分多钟的时间里，我们的17位朋友被夺走了生命，15人受伤，道格拉斯社区的每一个人，绝对是每一个人，都永远地改变了。

sentences.en: There was a real, what seemed like, conversation happening in Washington.
sentences.zh: 当时华盛顿确实发生了一场看似有意义的对话。

sentences.en: Don't worry about the NRA.
sentences.zh: 别担心全国步枪协会（NRA）。

sentences.en: They're on our side.
sentences.zh: 他们站在我们这边。

sentences.en: You guys, half of you are so afraid of the NRA.
sentences.zh: 你们这些人，有一半人太害怕全国步枪协会了。

sentences.en: There's nothing to be afraid of.
sentences.zh: 没什么好怕的。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: If they're not with you, we have to fight them every once in a while.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不站在你这边，我们偶尔就得和他们斗争。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: But there might actually be some change.
sentences.zh: 但可能真的会有一些改变。

sentences.en: I will tell you, they are doing what they think is right.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉你，他们正在做他们认为正确的事情。

sentences.en: But sometimes we're going to have to be very tough, and we're going to have to fight them.
sentences.zh: 但有时我们必须非常强硬，我们必须与他们斗争。

sentences.en: But we need strong background checks.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要强有力的背景调查。

sentences.en: But interestingly to me, as a columnist who covers business and finance in the world of Wall Street, there was one group that nobody was focused on.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，作为一名报道华尔街商业和金融界的专栏作家，我发现有一个群体没人关注。

sentences.en: And that was this business community that was supporting the gun industry.
sentences.zh: 那就是支持枪支行业的商业界。

sentences.en: And I started to think to myself, Washington may or may not get there.
sentences.zh: 我开始对自己说，华盛顿可能会也可能不会采取行动。

sentences.en: And of course, they didn't.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们没有。

sentences.en: But here's a group of people who have real influence.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一群真正有影响力的人。

sentences.en: If you follow the money, you can really start to see this remarkable ecosystem, which has supported the gun industry.
sentences.zh: 如果你追踪资金流向，你真的可以开始看到这个支持枪支行业的非凡生态系统。

sentences.en: And I spent virtually the past year and a half regularly writing columns, effectively laying out all of the different players in this ecosystem
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年半里，我几乎一直在定期撰写专栏，实际上列出了这个生态系统中所有不同的参与者，

sentences.en: and also address the kinds of roles and opportunities that existed for these companies to play in trying to end gun violence.
sentences.zh: 同时也探讨了这些公司在试图终结枪支暴力方面所拥有的角色和机会。

sentences.en: And tell me about this ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这个生态系统。

sentences.en: Describe it to me.
sentences.zh: 描述一下。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, people think that there's just gun makers.
sentences.zh: 人们认为只有枪支制造商。

sentences.en: But there's all of the suppliers to the gun maker.
sentences.zh: 但还有枪支制造商的所有供应商。

sentences.en: There are distributors.
sentences.zh: 有分销商。

sentences.en: There are retailers.
sentences.zh: 有零售商。

sentences.en: There are credit card companies, credit card networks, credit card processors.
sentences.zh: 有信用卡公司、信用卡网络、信用卡处理商。

sentences.en: There are banks behind all of these institutions.
sentences.zh: 所有这些机构背后都有银行。

sentences.en: Everybody's playing a role.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在扮演一个角色。

sentences.en: There are investors.
sentences.zh: 还有投资者。

sentences.en: And I took the position that there was an opportunity for these companies to do something here.
sentences.zh: 我的立场是，这些公司在这里有机会做点什么。

sentences.en: And what exactly was the opportunity you were asking them to take?
sentences.zh: 你要求他们采取的机会到底是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the first part was just to acknowledge that they were part of the ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第一部分只是承认他们是生态系统的一部分。

sentences.en: So many of them didn't even want to acknowledge that they had anything to do with this.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人甚至不想承认自己与此事有任何关系。

sentences.en: Most people didn't even see the connections or ties.
sentences.zh: 大多数人甚至没有看到其中的联系或纽带。

sentences.en: Nobody would ever say a shooting that happened in a high school has something to do with a bank that happens to be located on Park Avenue.
sentences.zh: 没有人会说发生在高中里的枪击事件与位于公园大道的银行有什么关系。

sentences.en: For example, in one of the columns that I worked on, we identified that in a majority of the mass shootings of the last decade in America, that they were financed by credit cards.
sentences.zh: 例如，在我撰写的一篇专栏文章中，我们发现过去十年美国发生的大多数大规模枪击事件都是通过信用卡资助的。

sentences.en: And then in many cases, the shooters could not have afforded the guns that were used if they didn't have access to the credit card.
sentences.zh: 而且在许多情况下，如果枪手没有信用卡，他们根本买不起所使用的枪支。

sentences.en: So the credit card itself became a key to the shooting.
sentences.zh: 所以信用卡本身成了枪击事件的关键。

sentences.en: And the banks became unwitting co-conspirators.
sentences.zh: 而银行成了不知情的共犯。

sentences.en: And, you know, some of this was inspired actually by what some of the online payment companies had already done.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，其中一些灵感实际上来自于一些在线支付公司已经做过的事情。

sentences.en: So companies like PayPal and Stripe and Square and even Apple Pay had explicit policies that said that they don't transact online for sales around guns and gun-related merchandise.
sentences.zh: 像PayPal、Stripe、Square甚至Apple Pay这样的公司都有明确的政策，规定他们不处理在线销售枪支和枪支相关商品的交易。

sentences.en: And I thought to myself, if they can make that decision, can't others.
sentences.zh: 我心想，如果他们能做出那个决定，其他人为什么不能呢？

sentences.en: And in addition to that, you'd already started to see some companies, including Walmart, take some early steps.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，你已经开始看到一些公司，包括沃尔玛，采取了一些早期措施。

sentences.en: So Walmart had instituted a new age limit, 21 years old, no longer just 18.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛实施了新的年龄限制，21岁，不再仅仅是18岁。

sentences.en: To buy a gun.
sentences.zh: 购买枪支。

sentences.en: To buy a gun.
sentences.zh: 购买枪支。

sentences.en: They had eliminated handguns from most of their stores.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在大多数门店取消了手枪销售。

sentences.en: And they'd eliminated AR-15s and other assault-style guns completely.
sentences.zh: 并且完全取消了AR-15和其他攻击性枪支的销售。

sentences.en: So explain how you imagine all these different actors working together so that ultimately there are fewer mass shootings, which is obviously the goal.
sentences.zh: 那么请解释一下你如何设想所有这些不同的参与者共同努力，从而最终减少大规模枪击事件，这显然是目标。

sentences.en: What exactly would retailers, banks, and credit card companies do?
sentences.zh: 零售商、银行和信用卡公司到底会做什么？

sentences.en: What does this look like in practice?
sentences.zh: 这在实践中是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Okay, so let me lay it out for you.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我为你梳理一下。

sentences.en: Let's say somebody that's planning a mass shooting decides they're going to buy two or three or four guns in the span of three or four weeks.
sentences.zh: 假设有人计划进行大规模枪击，决定在三到四周内购买两、三或四把枪。

sentences.en: And then they go online and they might buy ammunition from somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 然后他们上网，可能会从别处购买弹药。

sentences.en: They might buy body armor.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会购买防弹衣。

sentences.en: You would think that the credit card industry, the banking industry, and all of those retailers could effectively track those sales.
sentences.zh: 你会认为信用卡行业、银行业和所有这些零售商可以有效地追踪这些销售。

sentences.en: And in the same way that banks today are looking for anti-money laundering
sentences.zh: 就像银行今天在寻找反洗钱

sentences.en: or are looking for human trafficking, they say to themselves, okay, this is a suspicious purchase.
sentences.zh: 或寻找人口贩运一样，他们对自己说，好吧，这是一笔可疑的购买。

sentences.en: They connect dots.
sentences.zh: 他们连接这些点。

sentences.en: They connect dots.
sentences.zh: 他们连接这些点。

sentences.en: This already exists.
sentences.zh: 这已经存在了。

sentences.en: They just don't do it for guns because they can't see the information.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不针对枪支这样做，因为他们看不到信息。

sentences.en: And they can't see the information because the retailers don't provide it and the networks haven't tried to create systems to allow for it.
sentences.zh: 他们看不到信息是因为零售商不提供，而网络也没有试图建立允许这样做的系统。

sentences.en: So it's a see no evil, hear no evil situation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种“非礼勿视，非礼勿听”的情况。

sentences.en: And you want that to change.
sentences.zh: 而你希望这种情况改变。

sentences.en: You want the financial system to treat guns the way it currently treats issues like drugs or money laundering.
sentences.zh: 你希望金融系统对待枪支的方式就像对待毒品或洗钱等问题一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I want to be 100% clear here.
sentences.zh: 我想在这里百分之百地明确一点。

sentences.en: The goal is not to prevent people from buying guns.
sentences.zh: 目标不是阻止人们购买枪支。

sentences.en: These are legal products.
sentences.zh: 这些是合法产品。
百分之百。

sentences.en: The goal is to identify suspicious purchasing activity and then to either try to stop it at the register or to report it so that law enforcement can take a second look.
sentences.zh: 目标是识别可疑的购买活动，然后要么试图在收银台阻止它，要么举报它，以便执法部门可以进行二次审查。

sentences.en: And so the real idea here is that if you could create this best practices sales approach, you could actually change the dynamic in a material way.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的真正想法是，如果你能建立这种最佳实践的销售方法，你实际上可以在实质上改变这种动态。

sentences.en: And as a columnist distinct from a reporter in the newsroom, it sounds like you are taking the position that there's a kind of moral obligation
sentences.zh: 作为一名不同于新闻编辑室记者的专栏作家，听起来你的立场是，在金融系统内部存在一种道德义务，

sentences.en: within the financial system that in your mind they have not been awakened to or are aware of, that they can and should play a role in restricting
sentences.zh: 在你看来，他们还没有意识到这一点，或者没有意识到他们可以而且应该在限制

sentences.en: or monitoring gun sales in light of these mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 或监控枪支销售方面发挥作用，鉴于这些大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It's a responsibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种责任。

sentences.en: Especially in an environment in which lawmakers seem so deadlocked on everything that nobody is willing to step up.
sentences.zh: 特别是在立法者似乎在所有问题上都陷入僵局，没有人愿意挺身而出的环境下。

sentences.en: So you're encouraging these companies to take what would be pretty big steps to tackle the question of gun control themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以你是在鼓励这些公司采取相当大的步骤，亲自解决枪支管制问题。

sentences.en: To basically go outside the bounds of what we, and I assume they, normally think of as the responsibilities of the private sector.
sentences.zh: 基本上是超越我们，我也假设他们，通常认为的私营部门的责任范围。

sentences.en: So do they actually do it?
sentences.zh: 那么他们真的会这样做吗？

sentences.en: Kind of.
sentences.zh: 算是吧。

sentences.en: We'll call it baby steps.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为小步快跑。

sentences.en: One of the country's biggest sporting goods retailers announced today that it will stop selling assault-style rifles, along with the sale of any guns, to those under 21.
sentences.zh: 全国最大的体育用品零售商之一今天宣布，将停止销售攻击性步枪，并停止向21岁以下的人销售任何枪支。

sentences.en: You had Dick's Sporting Goods come out.
sentences.zh: 迪克体育用品公司（Dick's Sporting Goods）站出来了。

sentences.en: We actually sold the shooter a shotgun in November of last year.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上在去年11月向枪手出售了一把猎枪。

sentences.en: And we looked at that and found out that we did this.
sentences.zh: 我们审视了这一点，发现我们确实做了这些事。

sentences.en: We had a pit in our stomach and said, we don't want to be a part of this story.
sentences.zh: 我们感到心里很不是滋味，并说，我们不想成为这个故事的一部分。

sentences.en: You had BlackRock, the largest investor in the world.
sentences.zh: 你看看贝莱德（BlackRock），全球最大的投资者。

sentences.en: BlackRock made public a letter with the questions that it is asking of gun makers and gun sellers.
sentences.zh: 贝莱德公开了一封信，信中提出了它向枪支制造商和销售商询问的问题。

sentences.en: Starts sending letters to gun manufacturers and gun retailers saying, what are you going to do about gun violence?
sentences.zh: 开始给枪支制造商和零售商发信，询问他们打算如何应对枪支暴力问题？

sentences.en: Questions range from litigation risks to gun safety to background checks.
sentences.zh: 问题涵盖了从诉讼风险到枪支安全，再到背景调查等各个方面。

sentences.en: Citigroup has said it's going to introduce new restrictions on business customers who sell guns.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团（Citigroup）表示，将对销售枪支的商业客户引入新的限制措施。

sentences.en: You had Citigroup and Bank of America say, we are no longer going to finance gun manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团和美国银行（Bank of America）都表示，我们将不再为枪支制造商提供融资。

sentences.en: We're no longer going to advise gun makers.
sentences.zh: 我们不再为枪支制造商提供咨询服务。

sentences.en: Citigroup will require clients not to sell firearms to anyone who hasn't passed a background test or anyone under the age of 21 and not to sell high capacity magazines.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团将要求客户不得向任何未通过背景调查的人或 21 岁以下的人出售枪支，也不得销售大容量弹匣。

sentences.en: They're no longer going to be our clients.
sentences.zh: 他们将不再是我们的客户。

sentences.en: So from your perspective, there is some momentum here.
sentences.zh: 所以从你的角度来看，这里确实有一些推动力。

sentences.en: A little momentum.
sentences.zh: 有一点推动力。

sentences.en: And it felt like there was going to be some even more momentum, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，当时感觉还会有更多的推动力。

sentences.en: But then everything stopped.
sentences.zh: 但随后一切都停止了。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: So Citigroup, which had announced that they were going to separate themselves from the gun makers,
sentences.zh: 花旗集团此前宣布他们将与枪支制造商划清界限，

sentences.en: this is now April 2018, some of their senior executives happened to go to a meeting with
sentences.zh: 那是 2018 年 4 月，他们的一些高管恰好去参加了一场会议，

sentences.en: commissioners from the SEC, which is the regulatory body that oversees these banks in large part.
sentences.zh: 与会者包括美国证券交易委员会（SEC）的委员，该机构在很大程度上是监管这些银行的监管机构。

sentences.en: And the meeting was not really supposed to be about guns at all.
sentences.zh: 而且这次会议本来根本不应该谈论枪支问题。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be about all sorts of esoteric regulations that relate to the banks themselves.
sentences.zh: 会议本应讨论与银行自身相关的各种深奥法规。

sentences.en: But at this meeting, one of the commissioners, a conservative commissioner, effectively said,
sentences.zh: 但在这次会议上，其中一位委员，一位保守派委员，实际上说，

sentences.en: we're not going to help you on any of these things because of the position you've taken on guns.
sentences.zh: 因为你们在枪支问题上的立场，我们不会在这些事情上提供任何帮助。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And once that got around Wall Street, everybody put their pens down.
sentences.zh: 一旦这个消息在华尔街传开，每个人都停下了手中的动作。

sentences.en: Goldman Sachs, in fact, was about to put out a public policy statement about the position they were going to take related to guns.
sentences.zh: 事实上，高盛（Goldman Sachs）当时正准备发布一份关于他们对枪支问题所持立场的公共政策声明。

sentences.en: But upon hearing what the SEC had done, they started to rethink their position.
sentences.zh: 但在听到 SEC 的所作所为后，他们开始重新考虑自己的立场。

sentences.en: So the message here is stay in your lane or else.
sentences.zh: 所以这里传达的信息是：管好你自己的事，否则后果自负。

sentences.en: It sounds a little bit like the message that supporters of gun rights...
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点像枪支权利支持者……

sentences.en: ...send to elected officials in Washington.
sentences.zh: ……发给华盛顿民选官员的信息。

sentences.en: In the case of the SEC, they effectively oversee these banks every single day.
sentences.zh: 就 SEC 而言，他们实际上每天都在监管这些银行。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so on the priority list of things that the banks are facing and dealing with...
sentences.zh: 所以，在银行面临和处理的优先事项清单上……

sentences.en: They can put guns in their back pocket.
sentences.zh: 他们可以把枪支问题抛在脑后。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, I used to get calls from CEOs and executives at all sorts of companies virtually every other day during that period.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在那段时期，我几乎每隔一天就会接到各种公司首席执行官和高管的电话。

sentences.en: But by the summer, those calls really started to trail off.
sentences.zh: 但到了夏天，这些电话真的开始减少了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So at this point, it feels like you have reached the end of your capacity to influence this
sentences.zh: 所以此时此刻，感觉你已经达到了影响此事的极限，

sentences.en: and the business world is realizing that the cost of engaging on guns is probably just too high.
sentences.zh: 而商界也意识到，参与枪支问题的代价可能实在太高了。

sentences.en: They're corporations.
sentences.zh: 他们是企业。

sentences.en: This is not their problem, especially if it's going to become a problem for them.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的问题，尤其是如果这会给他们带来麻烦的话。

sentences.en: Well, I hadn't given up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我没有放弃。

sentences.en: And sadly, the shootings didn't stop either.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，枪击事件也没有停止。

sentences.en: We began with breaking news.
sentences.zh: 我们从突发新闻开始报道。

sentences.en: A deadly mass shooting at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州埃尔帕索市一家沃尔玛超市发生致命的大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: The numbers are staggering.
sentences.zh: 数字令人震惊。

sentences.en: So we had this terrible massacre at a Walmart store in El Paso where 22 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 我们在埃尔帕索的一家沃尔玛超市发生了这场可怕的屠杀，造成 22 人死亡。

sentences.en: And it was at that point where I went back to the computer.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我回到了电脑前。

sentences.en: And this time, I decided I was going to write an open letter to Doug McMillan, the CEO of Walmart,
sentences.zh: 这一次，我决定写一封公开信给沃尔玛首席执行官道格·麦克米伦（Doug McMillan），

sentences.en: to effectively say to him, you have an authentic claim in a way that no other CEO in the country does to address this and to engage in a conversation about gun violence in America
sentences.zh: 实际上是想对他说，你比国内任何其他首席执行官都更有正当理由来解决这个问题，并参与关于美国枪支暴力的对话，

sentences.en: because of what had just happened in the store.
sentences.zh: 因为刚刚在你的店里发生了那样的事情。

sentences.en: But you also have now a moral responsibility to try to end this.
sentences.zh: 但你现在也有道德责任去尝试终结这一切。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Andrew, after the shooting in El Paso, you decide to go directly to the CEO of Walmart.
sentences.zh: 那么，安德鲁，在埃尔帕索枪击事件后，你决定直接去找沃尔玛的首席执行官。

sentences.en: What do you say in this letter to him?
sentences.zh: 你在信中对他说了什么？

sentences.en: I was effectively saying to him, you have leverage over the gun makers.
sentences.zh: 我实际上是在对他说，你对枪支制造商有影响力。

sentences.en: You have leverage over lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 你对立法者有影响力。

sentences.en: You have leverage over the financial industry.
sentences.zh: 你对金融行业有影响力。

sentences.en: Go to them, talk to them, force them to engage in a conversation about what everybody can do to fix this.
sentences.zh: 去找他们，和他们谈谈，迫使他们参与关于每个人能做些什么来解决这个问题的对话。

sentences.en: Walmart is famous for squeezing people on the issues that they care about.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛以在他们关心的问题上向人们施压而闻名。

sentences.en: And my view was this was now an issue that they had to care about.
sentences.zh: 而我的观点是，这现在是一个他们必须关心的问题。

sentences.en: So after I wrote the letter, a couple days later, Doug McMillan posted a memo, which he also sent me, as a letter to his employees.
sentences.zh: 所以在我写完信几天后，道格·麦克米伦发布了一份备忘录，他也把它作为一封信发给了我，发给了他的员工。

sentences.en: And in that letter said that he had heard from a lot of people throughout the country about this issue of gun violence and said that he wanted to take some time to try to figure out what Walmart can or should do.
sentences.zh: 在那封信中，他说他听到了全国各地许多人关于枪支暴力问题的声音，并表示他想花点时间弄清楚沃尔玛能做什么或应该做什么。

sentences.en: And what's your sense of what he's likely to do, given what Walmart is and his role?
sentences.zh: 考虑到沃尔玛的性质和他的角色，你觉得他可能会做什么？

sentences.en: You know, I've covered Walmart and Doug McMillan for a long time now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我报道沃尔玛和道格·麦克米伦已经很长时间了。

sentences.en: And you could tell that he has always struggled with this issue of how far to go.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出，他一直在这个问题上挣扎，不知道该走多远。

sentences.en: You know, this is a company that's based in Arkansas.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一家总部位于阿肯色州的公司。

sentences.en: This is a red state.
sentences.zh: 这是一个红州（共和党票仓）。

sentences.en: And any public statement that he were to make on a polarizing issue in America could have a backlash on the business.
sentences.zh: 他在美国任何一个两极分化的问题上发表的任何公开声明，都可能对业务产生反弹。

sentences.en: And he'd seen it.
sentences.zh: 他见过这种情况。

sentences.en: He'd watched it happen.
sentences.zh: 他亲眼目睹了这一切的发生。

sentences.en: Again, when Dix announced they were no longer going to sell assault style guns, there was a massive backlash.
sentences.zh: 同样，当迪克体育用品（Dick's）宣布他们将不再销售突击步枪时，遭到了巨大的反弹。

sentences.en: There were boycotts.
sentences.zh: 出现了抵制活动。

sentences.en: Earnings went down.
sentences.zh: 收益下降了。

sentences.en: The stock price went down.
sentences.zh: 股价下跌了。

sentences.en: You know, when Citigroup made their announcement, there were people cutting up their credit cards and posting pictures of it on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当花旗集团宣布他们的决定时，有人剪掉了他们的信用卡，并把照片发到了推特上。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of reasons for him to be cautious on this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以他在这个问题上保持谨慎是有很多原因的。

sentences.en: And yet this week you get this email saying that Doug McMillan, CEO of Walmart, has decided to come out and take these steps around ammunition, around stopping certain gun sales,
sentences.zh: 然而本周你收到了这封电子邮件，说沃尔玛首席执行官道格·麦克米伦决定站出来，在弹药方面、在停止某些枪支销售方面采取这些措施，

sentences.en: around going to Congress and saying you should be thinking about an assault weapons ban.
sentences.zh: 在去国会说你们应该考虑禁止攻击性武器方面采取行动。

sentences.en: And this was dramatic because up until this point, Walmart, even when they had taken steps to remove AR-15s, for example, from their stores,
sentences.zh: 这非常引人注目，因为在此之前，沃尔玛即使在采取措施将 AR-15 等枪支从商店中移除时，

sentences.en: had never said that the reason they were doing it was for social issues.
sentences.zh: 也从未说过他们这样做是因为社会问题。

sentences.en: The reason was always about the marketplace or something else.
sentences.zh: 原因总是关于市场或其他什么。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, the CEO of the largest retailer in America is talking about gun violence as a problem.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，美国最大零售商的首席执行官开始谈论枪支暴力是一个问题。

sentences.en: The status quo is no longer acceptable.
sentences.zh: 现状已不再被接受。

sentences.en: So how do you understand his decision?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何理解他的决定？

sentences.en: Well, I think when 22 people die in your store, it really makes you rethink what you're willing to say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为当 22 个人死在你的店里时，这真的会让你重新思考你愿意说什么。

sentences.en: I also think there's a shift in public opinion in this country towards more gun control and background checks and reasonable sales processes than there has been in a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我还认为，这个国家的公众舆论正在发生转变，比过去很长一段时间都更倾向于加强枪支管制、背景调查和合理的销售流程。

sentences.en: And most of what he's proposed, frankly, is not that controversial at all.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，他提出的大部分建议一点也不具争议性。

sentences.en: In fact, a lot of critics would say it hasn't gone far enough.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多批评者会说这还远远不够。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about what it actually will be doing, these moves that he's just announced.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈他刚刚宣布的这些举措实际上会做什么。

sentences.en: What's the practical impact of them?
sentences.zh: 它们的实际影响是什么？

sentences.en: Well, let's take what Walmart's doing on ammunition.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们看看沃尔玛在弹药方面正在做什么。

sentences.en: They sell 20 percent of all the ammunition.
sentences.zh: 他们销售了所有弹药的 20%。

sentences.en: Doug McMillan is now saying that after these policies are put in place, they'll sell somewhere between six and nine percent of the ammunition in the country.
sentences.zh: 道格·麦克米伦现在表示，在这些政策实施后，他们将销售全国 6% 到 9% 的弹药。

sentences.en: So cut down by more than more than half in Washington.
sentences.zh: 所以在华盛顿减少了一半以上。

sentences.en: He's writing letters directly to the president.
sentences.zh: 他直接给总统写信。

sentences.en: He's writing letters directly to Congress saying we are asking you to have a debate around the assault weapon ban.
sentences.zh: 他直接给国会写信，说我们请求你们围绕攻击性武器禁令进行辩论。

sentences.en: That's real.
sentences.zh: 那是真实的。

sentences.en: When the CEO of the largest retailer in the country, which, by the way, is also one of the biggest lobbyists in Washington, speaks, people listen.
sentences.zh: 当全国最大零售商的首席执行官——顺便说一句，他也是华盛顿最大的游说者之一——开口说话时，人们会倾听。

sentences.en: So what's the impact of it?
sentences.zh: 那么它的影响是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's something, but it's not everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这算是一点影响，但不是全部。

sentences.en: The question is whether it now gives license to the rest of corporate America to join him.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这是否现在给了美国其他企业加入他的许可。

sentences.en: If that happens, we might actually look back at this as a tipping point.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，我们回头看时，可能会将其视为一个转折点。

sentences.en: And the rest of corporate America is watching literally right now to see what's going to happen to Walmart.
sentences.zh: 而美国其他企业现在正盯着看沃尔玛会发生什么。

sentences.en: Our customer is going to flee.
sentences.zh: 我们的客户会逃离吗？

sentences.en: What's the real economic impact of what they've done?
sentences.zh: 他们所做之事的真正经济影响是什么？

sentences.en: And what has been the reaction?
sentences.zh: 反应如何？

sentences.en: Well, as you'd imagine, the NRA came out with a statement blasting the company.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所料，美国全国步枪协会（NRA）发表了一份声明抨击该公司。

sentences.en: Within hours of the announcement, the NRA tweeted, it is shameful to see Walmart succumb to the pressures of the anti-gun elites.
sentences.zh: 在宣布后的几个小时内，NRA 发推文称，看到沃尔玛屈服于反枪支精英的压力是可耻的。

sentences.en: Lines at Walmart will soon be replaced by lines at other retailers who are more supportive of America's fundamental freedoMs.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛的排队人群很快就会被那些更支持美国基本自由的其他零售商的排队人群所取代。

sentences.en: You have some customers on Twitter with a hashtag, boycott Walmart.
sentences.zh: 你在推特上看到一些客户带着“抵制沃尔玛”的标签。

sentences.en: Walmart, what are y'all doing?
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛，你们在干什么？

sentences.en: Y'all think that by telling me and other people that have a license to carry that you can't bring a gun into Walmart is going to stop a man shooting?
sentences.zh: 你们以为告诉我和其他有持枪证的人说不能带枪进沃尔玛，就能阻止一个人开枪吗？

sentences.en: Huh?
sentences.zh: 哈？

sentences.en: That's not going to stop nothing.
sentences.zh: 那什么也阻止不了。

sentences.en: Are y'all stupid?
sentences.zh: 你们是不是傻？

sentences.en: At the other extreme, you have people giving them attaboys, saying, this is great.
sentences.zh: 在另一个极端，有人给他们点赞，说这太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm now going to shop at Walmart.
sentences.zh: 我现在要去沃尔玛购物。

sentences.en: And to the extent that people look at the price of the stock as an indicator about what's going to happen to the company and the company's sales, well, the stock actually went up.
sentences.zh: 如果人们把股价作为公司和销售额未来走势的指标，那么股价实际上是上涨的。

sentences.en: I find myself struck that the biggest employer in the country has responded at least a bit to this call that you put out.
sentences.zh: 我感到震惊的是，这个国家最大的雇主至少对你发出的这个呼吁做出了一点回应。

sentences.en: But what you have been advocating for and many others is a lot bigger than a single company ending the sales of ammunition or even ending the sales of certain guns.
sentences.zh: 但你和其他许多人所倡导的，远不止是一家公司停止销售弹药或停止销售某些枪支那么简单。

sentences.en: It's this coordinated attempt to use the financial system to change basically the very nature of the gun industry.
sentences.zh: 这是一种协调一致的尝试，利用金融体系从根本上改变枪支行业的本质。

sentences.en: And are you seeing any signs that that is happening, that larger structural change?
sentences.zh: 你是否看到了任何迹象表明这种情况正在发生，即那种更大的结构性变革？

sentences.en: You know, for the most part, we're not there yet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很大程度上，我们还没有达到那个地步。

sentences.en: Credit card companies still, for the most part, don't see this as their issue.
sentences.zh: 信用卡公司在很大程度上仍然不认为这是他们的问题。

sentences.en: Some of the banks, some of the retailers are trying to figure out what they can do, but they're all anxious.
sentences.zh: 一些银行、一些零售商正在试图弄清楚他们能做什么，但他们都很焦虑。

sentences.en: They're all nervous.
sentences.zh: 他们都很紧张。

sentences.en: And that's why what Doug McMillan did may or may not be important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么道格·麦克米伦所做的事情可能重要，也可能不重要。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: You know, to gun rights supporters,
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于枪支权利支持者来说，

sentences.en: I have to imagine that what you're outlining sounds like you asking the financial system to do what lawmakers in Washington haven't done and may never do in their minds for good reason,
sentences.zh: 我不得不想象，你所概述的内容听起来就像是你要求金融体系去做华盛顿的立法者没有做过，而且在他们看来可能永远也不会做的事情，这倒是有充分理由的，

sentences.en: which is that it may inevitably infringe on their rights to buy guns.
sentences.zh: 那就是这可能会不可避免地侵犯他们购买枪支的权利。

sentences.en: Look, I hear that.
sentences.zh: 看，我听到了。

sentences.en: I see it in my Twitter feed every single day.
sentences.zh: 我每天在我的推特动态里都能看到。

sentences.en: But there's a crisis going on in this country.
sentences.zh: 但这个国家正在发生一场危机。

sentences.en: And the question is how we can confront the crisis.
sentences.zh: 问题是我们如何面对这场危机。

sentences.en: None of this is about flouting the law.
sentences.zh: 这一切都不是为了藐视法律。

sentences.en: None of this is about infringing on Second Amendment rights in any way.
sentences.zh: 这一切都不是为了以任何方式侵犯宪法第二修正案的权利。

sentences.en: This is about putting common sense protections on the sales of guns.
sentences.zh: 这是关于在枪支销售上设置常识性的保护措施。

sentences.en: Reasonable questions should be asked when suspicious behavior occurs.
sentences.zh: 当出现可疑行为时，应该提出合理的问题。

sentences.en: But I have to ask, should any of this that you've been advocating for, should it actually happen?
sentences.zh: 但我必须问，你所倡导的这一切，真的应该发生吗？

sentences.en: Do we really want private corporations, banks, credit cards, big financial firms, retailers, do we want them being the arbiters of this kind of a decision about what guns are sold,
sentences.zh: 我们真的希望私营企业、银行、信用卡公司、大型金融公司、零售商，我们希望他们成为决定销售何种枪支的仲裁者吗？

sentences.en: what ammunition is sold?
sentences.zh: 销售的是什么弹药？

sentences.en: Are you and others asking companies to be something that they really aren't and perhaps never should be in the United States, which is basically a stand-in for the government?
sentences.zh: 你和其他人是否在要求企业去扮演某种它们本非如此，甚至在美国可能永远不该扮演的角色，即基本上充当政府的替代者？

sentences.en: Because as we talked about with you recently, when a bunch of CEOs debated their role, how civic-minded they should be, at the end of the day, they're companies.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们最近和你谈到的，当一群首席执行官讨论他们的角色、他们应该有多大的公民意识时，归根结底，他们是企业。

sentences.en: They're for-profit businesses.
sentences.zh: 他们是营利性企业。

sentences.en: They're not elected officials.
sentences.zh: 他们不是民选官员。

sentences.en: They're not advocacy groups.
sentences.zh: 他们不是倡导团体。

sentences.en: So why should they be doing any of this stuff?
sentences.zh: 那么他们为什么要参与这些事情呢？

sentences.en: Look, companies make decisions every single day about what products they're going to put on their shelves, who they're going to do business with,
sentences.zh: 听着，企业每天都在做决定，决定把什么产品放在货架上，决定与谁做生意，

sentences.en: who they're going to provide loans to, for all sorts of different reasons.
sentences.zh: 决定向谁提供贷款，这些都是出于各种不同的原因。

sentences.en: People are making these decisions constantly.
sentences.zh: 人们一直在做这些决定。

sentences.en: So the idea that companies are supposed to actually just sit on their hands is crazy to me.
sentences.zh: 所以认为企业应该袖手旁观的想法在我看来很疯狂。

sentences.en: It's absolutely insanity to think that they are not supposed to have any responsibility in all of this.
sentences.zh: 认为他们不应该在这一切中承担任何责任，这绝对是疯了。

sentences.en: But if they take on this role that you're suggesting, are you worried that it'll, in a very real way,
sentences.zh: 但如果你建议他们承担这个角色，你是否担心这会以一种非常现实的方式，

sentences.en: let the government off the hook for playing a regulatory role we traditionally think of the government playing, of protecting the people?
sentences.zh: 让政府逃避其传统上被认为应该承担的监管角色，即保护人民的责任？

sentences.en: In a perfect world, the government would put in place reasonable and responsible regulations that would prevent this from happening.
sentences.zh: 在一个完美的世界里，政府会出台合理且负责任的法规来防止这种情况发生。

sentences.en: But by default, let's just agree that the laws on the books are not working.
sentences.zh: 但默认情况下，我们还是承认现有的法律行不通吧。

sentences.en: If they were, we wouldn't be having this conversation.
sentences.zh: 如果行得通，我们就不会有这场对话了。

sentences.en: If you take that as fact, the question is, what are you going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 如果你把这一点当作事实，问题就是，你打算怎么处理？

sentences.en: And if Washington is not going to do something about it, the question is, who?
sentences.zh: 如果华盛顿不打算采取行动，问题就是，谁来做？

sentences.en: What is the moral responsibility of business leaders to deal with very human issues?
sentences.zh: 商业领袖在处理非常人性化的问题上有什么道德责任？

sentences.en: And I think they have some.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们是有一些责任的。

sentences.en: Andrew, thank you.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Incidents over these past two months have shocked and saddened Hong Kong people.
sentences.zh: 过去两个月发生的事件令香港民众感到震惊和悲伤。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the chief executive of Hong Kong, Carrie Lam, said she would withdraw an unpopular extradition bill that has ignited months of massive protests across the city.
sentences.zh: 周三，香港行政长官林郑月娥表示，她将撤回一项不受欢迎的引渡法案，该法案已在全港引发了数月的大规模抗议活动。

sentences.en: Our foremost priority now is to end violence, to safeguard the rule of law, and to restore order and safety in society.
sentences.zh: 我们现在的首要任务是结束暴力，维护法治，恢复社会秩序和安全。

sentences.en: The bill would have allowed for citizens of Hong Kong to be tried for crimes in mainland China,
sentences.zh: 该法案本允许将香港公民送往中国内地接受审判，

sentences.en: sparking fears that China might have used the law as a way to prosecute and silence its critics in Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 这引发了人们的担忧，即中国可能会利用该法律作为在香港起诉和压制批评者的手段。

sentences.en: The withdrawal of the bill was a major demand of the protesters, but it's unclear whether Lamb's decision will end the demonstrations,
sentences.zh: 撤回法案是抗议者的主要诉求之一，但目前尚不清楚林郑月娥的决定是否会结束示威活动，

sentences.en: which have since expanded to encompass broader grievances against her government.
sentences.zh: 因为示威活动已经扩大到涵盖对她政府更广泛的不满。

sentences.en: Order, questions to the prime minister, Siobhan McDonough.
sentences.zh: 肃静，首相问答环节，希沃恩·麦克唐纳。

sentences.en: For the second day in a row, British lawmakers rejected the will of their new prime minister, Boris Johnson,
sentences.zh: 英国议员连续第二天否决了新任首相鲍里斯·约翰逊的意愿，

sentences.en: by voting to stop him from leaving the European Union by the end of the month without a negotiated deal.
sentences.zh: 投票阻止他在本月底前在没有达成协议的情况下脱离欧盟。

sentences.en: Yet the prime minister pursues a game of brinkmanship built on the livelihoods, health and future of my constituents and our country.
sentences.zh: 然而，首相却在拿我选民和我们国家的生计、健康和未来进行一场边缘政策博弈。

sentences.en: The showdown over Brexit has triggered a civil war inside Johnson's Conservative Party, as members of his own party turn against him, calling his plan dangerous for Britain.
sentences.zh: 围绕英国脱欧的摊牌引发了约翰逊保守党内部的内战，他自己党内的成员也倒戈反对他，称他的计划对英国来说是危险的。

sentences.en: But Johnson vowed to press on with his strategy.
sentences.zh: 但约翰逊誓言要继续推进他的战略。

sentences.en: Prime Minister, Mr. Speaker, as the Honourable Lady knows very well, this government will take this country out of the European Union on October the 31St.
sentences.zh: 首相，议长先生，正如这位尊敬的女士非常清楚的那样，本届政府将于10月31日带领这个国家脱离欧盟。

sentences.en: Finally.
sentences.zh: 终于。

sentences.en: Parts of Abaco are decimated.
sentences.zh: 阿巴科的部分地区被摧毁了。

sentences.en: The national airport in Abaco is underwater.
sentences.zh: 阿巴科的国家机场被淹没在水下。

sentences.en: The runway is completely flooded.
sentences.zh: 跑道完全被淹了。

sentences.en: And in fact, the area around the airport now looks like a lake.
sentences.zh: 事实上，机场周围的区域现在看起来像个湖。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the full devastation of Hurricane Dorian was revealed in the Bahamas, where government officials said it had destroyed thousands of buildings,
sentences.zh: 周三，飓风“多里安”造成的全面破坏在巴哈马显现出来，政府官员称飓风摧毁了数千座建筑物，

sentences.en: wiped out entire neighborhoods, and killed at least 20 people.
sentences.zh: 夷平了整个社区，并造成至少20人死亡。

sentences.en: Wow, this is Lenny's house.
sentences.zh: 哇，这是莱尼的房子。

sentences.en: Used to be Lenny's house.
sentences.zh: 曾经是莱尼的房子。

sentences.en: What's left of it?
sentences.zh: 还剩下什么？

sentences.en: Firefly.
sentences.zh: 萤火虫。

sentences.en: A lot of roof damage.
sentences.zh: 屋顶损坏严重。

sentences.en: The hurricane, now traveling parallel to the east coast of the United States as a Category 2 storm, is now forecast to close in on Charleston, South Carolina,
sentences.zh: 这场飓风目前正以二级风暴的强度沿着美国东海岸平行移动，预计将于今天晚些时候逼近南卡罗来纳州的查尔斯顿。

sentences.en: by later this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，安吉拉。

sentences.en: Thanks, Angela.
sentences.zh: 下周见。

sentences.en: I'll see you next week.
sentences.zh: 下周见。
